_source: Branch Education Short 'The Most Expensive Machine Ever Made', watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-18: frames every ~3-5 s, sentence timings and word counts from the transcript panel (not kept; its timestamps are coarse, so line times are approximate). The factory-cost figure shot near 44-48 s was not caught on a frame. Our own descriptions.

hook.firstFrame: a blurred close-up of machinery with a rainbow lens glow, before the first object comes into focus
hook.firstLine: Asks which machine in the world costs the most

shots.picture: out-of-focus machinery with a rainbow glow, racking into focus
a giant excavator on a blue gradient; a stack of banknotes grows below it with a green price counting up
a rocket lands in the same spot; the cash stack grows and the price counts on
a fighter jet replaces the rocket; the stack grows again
the chip-printing machine on a plinth with a crown above it and the biggest stack below
a single-car garage slides next to the machine to compare their sizes
a light beam paints a rainbow chip pattern across a wafer above the machine
the machine cut open with round inset bubbles showing its main modules, each labelled
a whole factory floor from above, rows of machines filling it
the factory with a framed thumbnail of the long video and a subscribe button over it

lines.gist: asks what the costliest machine in the world is
climbs a price ladder of famous big machines
names the chip-printing machine as the priciest of all
it is garage-sized and prints a chip's pattern across a wafer
a chip factory holds dozens of them, so the whole plant costs far more
points to the long video and asks for a subscribe

ending.cta: watch the full video and subscribe
ending.lastFrame: factory floor with a framed long-video thumbnail and a subscribe button

whyItWorks: a price ladder: each famous machine swaps into the same spot while a cash pile grows beneath it, so the last price lands hardest
one shared stage (blue gradient, grid floor) keeps every swap readable as a comparison
size made concrete by sliding an everyday object (a garage) next to the machine
inset bubbles around a cut-open machine name its parts at once without leaving the shot
